calls.head: Special teams tilt toward Edmonton
calls.body: Vancouver’s penalty kill sits 27th of 32, and Edmonton’s power play is 1st (9.6 expected goals per 60).
calls.call: Edmonton’s power play creates at least its usual 9.6 expected goals per 60.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Edmonton’s power play created 11.0 expected goals per 60 in 6:48 of 5-on-4 time, against its usual 9.6, and scored 2 goals.

calls.head: Edmonton gets to the dangerous areas
calls.body: Vancouver has struggled to keep shots to the perimeter (31st of 32), and Edmonton makes its shots count: one expected goal for every 15.3 unblocked shots, 8th in the league.
calls.call: Edmonton needs no more than its usual 15.3 unblocked shots per expected goal.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Edmonton needed 17.5 unblocked shots per expected goal, against its usual 15.3.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only a 32% chance, and it went the way we feared.

EDM.head: We gave Edmonton a 68% chance, and Edmonton delivered.

surprises.head: A rough night for D. Levi
surprises.body: D. Levi allowed 7 goals on shots worth 2.8 expected goals, 4.2 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 200 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Vancouver got to the dangerous areas
surprises.body: Vancouver needed 9.9 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 16.7 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 175 games.

surprises.head: Edmonton tried a different line
surprises.body: C. McDavid, L. Draisaitl, V. Podkolzin played 12:01 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Edmonton’s usual lines.
